the olfactory sensory placode is derived from placodal cells that have migrated from the anterior neural plate, and the olfactory sensory neurons are generated from these placodal cells and not from cranial neural crest.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the olfactory system forms through the interaction between two cell populations, the olfactory placodes and cranial neural crests.
the OP forms through cell movement and not cell division, and that there is limited cell mixing between the OP and the CNCCs.

the olfactory system is a complex sensory system that requires the cooperation of multiple embryonic cell populations to form, but these cells are not intermixed during the formation of the olfactory sensory organs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no cell mixing between the OP precursor cells and the cranial neural crest (CNCCs).
cell mixing between the neural crest and olfactory placode does not appear to occur during development, and therefore, the olfactory placodes do not appear to be a mixed lineage.
